goal: Make the first visit to a Docket project self-explanatory.

entries.title: 1. Project overview and getting started
entries.description:
Entry 1 of 4 in the first-time project experience roadmap: Project overview and getting started. It covers audit recommendations M1 and M2 and adds an Overview nav entry. Right now the project home (src/app/p/[projectSlug]/page.tsx) is just a heading and the line "Pick a section from the navigation to get started". Build a real project home with:
- A PageHeader showing the project name, its time zone, the viewer's role and one primary action.
- A Getting started checklist that works out its own state from the data. Steps: connect an account, add posting slots, write and schedule a first post. Optional steps: a voice profile, media, invite a teammate. Owners also get a server-setup row that links to the docs instead of printing commands. Once the required steps are done, the checklist collapses to a one-line "Setup complete". There is no stored dismissal.
- Sections for Needs attention, Coming up, Accounts, Posts by status and Content tools. Each has a populated view and an empty state whose action is the next dependent step, e.g. "You don't have any accounts yet — add one" or "No scheduled posts yet — write one".
- A Skeleton loading state.
- The browser tab title set to the project name.
- Overview as the first nav item, with an exact-match active state so /p/x does not prefix-match every route.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/onboarding.md in full, especially its opening Goal and Source paragraphs and the "Rules for every entry" list. Then read docs/research/onboarding-audit.md in full, especially recommendations M1 and M2. They give the exact header copy and primary-action logic, which service counts feed Needs attention, the checklist's structure, steps, editor behaviour and which docs the server-setup row links to, and the data gap on slot counts. The audit was written against the code of 2026-10-08, before the video roadmap landed, so re-check every line it cites against the current code. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill.

The roadmap's rules for every entry apply here:
- Leave the repo working, and say what the entry does not do and which later entry owns it.
- Never derive a person's name from their email; show member display names only.
- Be role-aware. Editors cannot manage accounts, slots or voice. Never show them actions they can't take, server commands or env var names; point them to the owners and admins by display name.
- Prefer the existing primitives: PageHeader, Card, EmptyState, Badge, StatusBadge, ProviderIcon, LocalTime, Skeleton, Alert, buttonStyles. Add a new shared component only where the audit says to (M2 allows a Checklist component), and document it in the design system.
- Keep the test-pinned labels: "Review (3)", ">Failures<", and Review above Failures in tests/integration/failures/nav.test.ts.
- Fold features that landed after the audit (activity history, problem notifications, video) into the overview rather than ignoring them.

Testing: component and integration tests for each section in both its empty and populated state, for an owner and an editor (editors see owner/admin display names, never emails, and no actions they can't take); the checklist deriving each step's status from data, collapsing to 'Setup complete' once required steps are done, and the owner-only server-setup row; the Overview nav item's exact-match active state; the tab title being the project name.

NOT included, as the roadmap states:
- Nav reordering (entry 3 owns nav order and grouping).
- Other routes' empty states (entry 2).
- Terminology (entry 3).
- Stored dismissal of the checklist. No entry in this roadmap owns it; entry 4 also excludes it because it needs a stored per-user preference and its own decision.
- A project-wide slot-count service. No later entry owns it; the audit says looping slots per account is fine for v1.
entries.rationale: First because it is the screen a newcomer lands on and fixes the reported confusion directly; the checklist it adds is what later entries link into.

entries.title: 2. Empty states that name the next step, and role awareness
entries.description:
Entry 2 of 4 in the first-time project experience roadmap: Empty states that name the next step, and role awareness. This is audit recommendation M3, applied across these routes:
- **Accounts:** role-aware copy; the connect section shown to managers only; unconfigured platforms collapsed for owners.
- **Calendar:** the empty state replaces the grid. When there are accounts but no slots, it says to add posting slots.
- **Compose:** explain before the click that Add to queue needs posting slots, with a link.
- **Posts, Failures and Review:** empty states that name the next step.
- **Generate and Jobs:** show every prerequisite at once. Env var names go to owners only.
- **Media:** hide the toolbar when the library is empty, and say "images and videos".
- **Voice:** an empty state that names the next step.
- **Scheduler-health banner:** editors get plain copy; owners get the commands.

EmptyState actions use buttonStyles, not underline links.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/onboarding.md in full, especially its opening Goal and Source paragraphs and the "Rules for every entry" list. Then read docs/research/onboarding-audit.md in full, especially section 3 (each destination when the project is empty), section 5 (what an editor sees) and recommendation M3. M3 gives the exact copy per route, the per-account hasActiveSlots read for Compose, the Jobs header and duplicate-action changes, the Alert replacements, and passing canManage to SchedulerHealth. The audit was written against the code of 2026-10-08, before the video roadmap landed, and Media, Compose and Accounts have changed since, so re-check every line it cites against the current code. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill.

The roadmap's rules for every entry apply here:
- Leave the repo working, and say what the entry does not do and which later entry owns it.
- Never derive a person's name from their email; show member display names only.
- Be role-aware. Editors cannot manage accounts, slots or voice. Never show them actions they can't take, server commands or env var names; point them to the owners and admins by display name.
- Prefer the existing primitives: PageHeader, Card, EmptyState, Badge, StatusBadge, ProviderIcon, LocalTime, Skeleton, Alert, buttonStyles. Add a new shared component only where the audit says to, and document it in the design system.
- Keep the test-pinned labels: "Review (3)", ">Failures<", and Review above Failures in tests/integration/failures/nav.test.ts.
- Fold features that landed after the audit (activity history, problem notifications, video) into these decisions rather than ignoring them.

Testing: for every route touched, a test of the empty state for an owner and for an editor, asserting the next-step action (or the owners/admins named for editors) and that editors never see env var names or server commands; Compose's slot hint before any click; Generate/Jobs listing every missing prerequisite at once; SchedulerHealth copy by role. Keep existing tests passing, including policy.test.tsx's ordering assertion.

NOT included, as the roadmap states:
- Renamed nav labels (entry 3).
- PageHeader descriptions (entry 3).
- The Accounts card restructure (entry 4).
entries.rationale: Second because once the overview points people to a destination, that destination must say what to do next; it reuses the role-aware patterns entry 1 establishes.

entries.title: 3. Terminology, page descriptions and nav order
entries.description:
Entry 3 of 4 in the first-time project experience roadmap: Terminology, page descriptions and nav order. This is audit recommendations S1 and S2.
- **Nav groups:** Overview / Publish (Compose, Calendar, Posts, Review, Failures) / Create (Generate, Brand voice, Media, Batch jobs) / Project (Accounts, Settings, and Activity if present).
- **Renames:** "Voice" becomes "Brand voice" and "Jobs" becomes "Batch jobs". Keep "Review" and "Failures". On the job page, "Targets" becomes "Accounts".
- **Page descriptions:** a one-line PageHeader description on every route.
- **Posting slot:** define the term once, by the slot editor.
- **Statuses:** show target statuses as readable words.
- **Help text:** role descriptions on the invite form, signup and invitations pages; hints on the voice editor; clearer /p/new copy and a time zone hint.
- **Docs:** update docs/design-system.md §6 and the docket-ui skill to match.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/onboarding.md in full, especially its opening Goal and Source paragraphs and the "Rules for every entry" list. Then read docs/research/onboarding-audit.md in full, especially section 6 (terms a newcomer won't know) and recommendations S1 and S2. They give the exact description copy per route, the posting-slot definition, the role-description wording, the voice-editor hint examples, the /p/new copy, and S2's instruction to check the tests for each string before changing it. The audit was written against the code of 2026-10-08, before the video roadmap landed, so re-check every line it cites against the current code. An Activity route now exists under src/app/p/[projectSlug]/activity. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill.

The roadmap's rules for every entry apply here:
- Leave the repo working, and say what the entry does not do and which later entry owns it.
- Never derive a person's name from their email; show member display names only.
- Be role-aware. Editors cannot manage accounts, slots or voice. Never show them actions they can't take, server commands or env var names; point them to the owners and admins by display name.
- Prefer the existing primitives: PageHeader, Card, EmptyState, Badge, StatusBadge, ProviderIcon, LocalTime, Skeleton, Alert, buttonStyles. Add a new shared component only where the audit says to, and document it in the design system.
- Keep the test-pinned labels: "Review (3)", ">Failures<", and Review directly above Failures in tests/integration/failures/nav.test.ts.
- Fold features that landed after the audit (activity history, problem notifications, video) into the nav decisions rather than ignoring them.

Testing: the nav groups and order (with Review directly above Failures), the renamed labels, a PageHeader description on every route, human-readable target statuses and role descriptions; update tests that assert old strings only where the rename is intended.

NOT included, as the roadmap states: showing or hiding nav items based on project state. The nav is a fixed list, and no later entry in this roadmap owns that.
entries.rationale: Third because renaming labels and adding page descriptions touches the same routes entry 2 changes; doing it after avoids rebasing copy twice.

entries.title: 4. Accounts restructure and first-post flow
entries.description:
Entry 4 of 4 in the first-time project experience roadmap: Accounts restructure and first-post flow. This is audit recommendations S3, C1, C3, C4 and C5.
- **Account cards (S3):** order each card as status, then posting slots, then posting instructions (collapsed), then remove.
- **After connecting (S3):** land on that account's slot editor.
- **SetupNotice (C1):** a SetupNotice variant for prerequisite lists.
- **First post (C3):** after a first schedule or publish, link to the calendar.
- **Getting-started page (C4):** a docs/getting-started.md page, linked from the entry-1 checklist.
- **Accessibility (C5):** the project switcher's accessible name without the shortcut, and the setup password hint linked with aria-describedby.

Before specifying, read .specify/roadmaps/onboarding.md in full, especially its opening Goal and Source paragraphs and the "Rules for every entry" list. Then read docs/research/onboarding-audit.md in full, especially section 7 (accessibility and mobile) and recommendations S3, C1, C3, C4 and C5. Points they cover:
- S3 says to send the owner to #account-{id} with the slot editor focused, and to check whether changing the connect-callback redirect counts as a behaviour change.
- C1 says SetupNotice is an EmptyState variant with a title and a list of prerequisites, for the Generate and Jobs gate checklist, and is added to design-system §7.
- C4 says to add the page to DocPage in src/lib/docs.ts.
- C5 gives the switcher fix (aria-hidden on the kbd, aria-keyshortcuts on the button) and the password-hint fix (aria-describedby, or use Field).

The audit was written against the code of 2026-10-08, before the video roadmap landed, and Accounts and Compose have changed since, so re-check every line it cites against the current code. Follow docs/design-system.md and the docket-ui skill.

The roadmap's rules for every entry apply here:
- Leave the repo working, and say what the entry does not do.
- Never derive a person's name from their email; show member display names only.
- Be role-aware. Editors cannot manage accounts, slots or voice. Never show them actions they can't take, server commands or env var names; point them to the owners and admins by display name.
- Prefer the existing primitives: PageHeader, Card, EmptyState, Badge, StatusBadge, ProviderIcon, LocalTime, Skeleton, Alert, buttonStyles. Add a new shared component only where the audit says to (C1 allows SetupNotice), and document it in the design system.
- Keep the test-pinned labels: "Review (3)", ">Failures<", and Review above Failures in tests/integration/failures/nav.test.ts.
- Fold features that landed after the audit (activity history, problem notifications, video) into these decisions rather than ignoring them.

Testing: the account card order, landing on the slot editor after connecting, SetupNotice listing prerequisites, the calendar link after a first schedule or publish, the getting-started doc linked from the checklist and present in the docs registry (mkdocs strict build passes), and the two accessibility fixes.

NOT included, as the roadmap states: a dismissible checklist (audit C2). It needs a stored per-user preference and its own decision. This is the last entry, so nothing in this roadmap owns it.
entries.rationale: Last: the 'should/could' polish that builds on entries 1 and 2 (the getting-started doc is linked from entry 1's checklist; SetupNotice formalises entry 2's prerequisite lists).
